topic: The Mystery of Pi in the Normal Distribution

sections.title: The Hook: Why does a Circle show up in Statistics?
lecture_lines: The bell curve: f(x) = C * e^(-x²/2).
Normalization constant C is 1/sqrt(2π).
Why does π appear in statistics?
Imagine darts landing on a target.
[Asset: BellCurveGraphic]
animations: Write formula: f(x) = C * e^(-x²/2). Color: #FFFFFF.
Highlight the symbol π in the formula. Color: #33FF57.

sections.title: Prerequisite: The Gaussian Integral
lecture_lines: Target: Gaussian integral I = ∫ e^(-x²) dx.
Elementary antiderivatives do not exist here.
Direct integration methods will fail.
animations: Display integral I = ∫ e^(-x²) dx. Color: #FFFFFF.
Draw integral curve highlighting area. Color: #3498DB.
Add red 'X' cross over integral sign. Color: #E74C3C.

sections.title: The 'Aha!' Moment: Polar Coordinates
lecture_lines: Square the integral: I² = ∫∫ e^-(x²+y²) dA.
Shift from Cartesian to polar coordinates.
Cartesian square grids morph into polar circles.
Variables: x²+y² = r².
[Asset: PolarCoordinateTransition]
animations: Show equation I² = ∫∫ e^-(x²+y²) dA. Color: #FFFFFF.
Display conversion formula: x = r cos θ, y = r sin θ. Color: #2ECC71.
Highlight area element dA = r dr dθ. Color: #9B59B6.
Update formula to polar form. Color: #FFFFFF.

sections.title: Solving the Integral
lecture_lines: Integrate over radius r and angle θ.
The 2π factor appears from integration.
This 2π is our hidden π source.
[Asset: RadarSweepAnimation]
animations: Show polar integral step using [Asset: /scratch/pawsey1357/jthen/Code2Video/assets/icon/radar.svg]. Color: #3498DB.

sections.title: Conclusion: Normalization
lecture_lines: Result: I² = π, so I = sqrt(π).
Total probability area must equal one.
The factor 1/sqrt(2π) scales the curve.
[Asset: NormalizationScalingGraphic]
animations: Show square root transformation I = sqrt(π). Color: #E74C3C.
